items.followUp: Differentiate between the functions of chloroplasts and leucoplasts.

rubric.why: Identifies the food-storage function of leucoplasts.
rubric.description: Leucoplasts store food, such as starch, oils or proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that leucoplasts store food or nutrients.

rubric.why: Identifies the pigment and colour-related function of chromoplasts.
rubric.description: Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments and give colour to plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromoplasts contain pigments or give colour.

modelAnswer: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food such as starch, oils or proteins.
Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments and give colour to flowers and fruits.

items.followUp: Give one way in which growing human populations can lead to deforestation.

rubric.why: Explains that population growth increases human demand.
rubric.description: As the human population increases, demand for land, food and other resources also increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting population growth with increased demand.

rubric.why: States that natural habitats are cleared to meet human needs.
rubric.description: Forests and other natural habitats are cleared to provide farmland, housing and resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that forests or other habitats are cleared to meet these demands.

modelAnswer: As the human population increases, the demand for land, food and other resources also increases.
Forests and other natural habitats are cleared to provide farmland, housing and resources.
